headline: High: Flowise can write shared workspace files while Notion AI reads workspace content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks in default collaborative setups.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can write to the server filesystem and handle uploaded files, while Notion AI reads workspace pages and databases. If Flowise outputs attacker-controlled text into shared content that Notion AI ingests, instructions can be smuggled across the pair. The path is plausible but not proven by docs alone, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Flowise writes untrusted content into a page or file that Notion AI later summarizes or answers over
IF Notion AI treats workspace text as instruction-bearing content without provenance filtering
mitigations: Restrict Flowise outputs to a quarantined folder or page
Add a manual review step before Notion AI ingests Flowise-generated text
Prefix Flowise outputs with machine-readable provenance labels
Use separate workspaces for generated content and human knowledge
requires-engineering: implement content provenance filtering between the systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, and has broad network egress to model providers and search/HTTP tools. Notion AI accesses workspace pages and team knowledge base content and sends data to vendor backends. Shared content can therefore flow from one agent into the other and onward to third parties, creating a default leakage path.
conditions: IF Flowise processes files containing sensitive workspace content
IF those outputs are pasted or synced into Notion pages that Notion AI can access
IF either backend retains or logs the transferred content
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of Flowise flows
Store generated artifacts in a separate workspace
Disable or minimize external tool calls in Flowise flows
Limit Notion AI access to non-sensitive pages
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before cross-system transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise can write the server filesystem and supports multiple instances with shared state via server datastore. Notion AI has shared workspace state across members but no host filesystem write. There is overlap on mutable content, but not the high-risk same-directory unrestricted write conflict described by the rubric, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both systems are configured to modify the same shared content store
IF Flowise writes artifacts that Notion AI also edits concurrently
mitigations: Separate writable storage locations
Assign one system as read-only for shared artifacts
Use timestamped filenames or page versions
Avoid concurrent edits to the same workspace object
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If Flowise-generated text is imported into Notion and then treated as authoritative, errors can cascade from generation to summarization or action. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Notion AI answers from Flowise-produced pages without human verification
IF Flowise outputs factual claims that are later reused as source material
mitigations: Mark Flowise outputs as unverified drafts
Require human review before publishing to Notion
Add source links next to generated claims
Use a checklist for factual assertions before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce citation validation in the workflow

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials, while Notion AI uses the invoking user's Notion workspace permissions and vendor backends. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different data classes and retention surfaces. That creates a compliance gap risk, though not enough evidence for medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Flowise flows and then copied into Notion workspaces
IF the workspace policy requires stricter retention or residency than either vendor path provides
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in cross-system workflows
Document which data classes may move between tools
Review vendor retention settings in both products
Limit Notion AI to non-regulated pages
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement and residency review
